description: Rounding, clamping, interpolation, and the default arguments that fill omitted parameters.

cases.name: int() truncates toward zero, which is not floor for negatives
floor(), int(), and ceil() all differ on a negative
sign() returns -1, 0, or 1, and sign(0) is 0
frac() subtracts the FLOOR, so a negative input yields a positive fraction
cases.note: frac(-0.25) is 0.75, not -0.25. An implementation using trunc() instead of floor() diverges on every negative.

cases.name: clamp() bounds a value to [lo, hi]
clamp() defaults its bounds to 0 and 1 when omitted
cases.note: Omitted arguments take the entry's declared defaults; they are not an error.

cases.name: clamp() with lo above hi returns hi
cases.note: Evaluated as min(max(v, lo), hi); the outer min wins. Not a documented MilkDrop case, but tiers must agree.

cases.name: min() and max() accept more than two arguments
mix() interpolates from the first toward the second, and lerp() is an alias
step() takes the edge FIRST and is 1 when the value reaches it
cases.note: step(edge, v) is v >= edge. Swapped arguments invert the result everywhere it is used.

cases.name: smoothstep() at the midpoint is one half
smoothstep() with equal edges degrades to a hard step
cases.note: Equal edges divide by zero. This platform defines the result as v < edge ? 0 : 1. WGSL and GLSL leave it undefined, so a GPU tier MUST special-case it rather than call the builtin.
